recognition: Recognized as UCI Beijing PM2.5 (UCI 381): hourly US Embassy PM2.5 paired with Beijing Capital Airport meteorology, 2010-2014. The supplied documentation cites Liang et al. (2015); no remembered result is claimed as new.
summary: R1 refined I1 to one index per observed high-PM2.5 episode and tested its six-hour continuation contrast. The computation found little matched difference and substantial uncertainty, so the directional prediction is unsupported in this dataset. Retain the question as a proposal for missingness-aware prospective replication, not as an established wind effect or operational rule. The limited title-only search does not resolve world-literature novelty.

candidates.title: When do wind-regime observations help characterize persistence of high-PM2.5 episodes?
candidates.question: For each observed episode of consecutive hourly PM2.5 >=150 ug/m^3, at its first hour with six subsequent consecutive observed hours, is six-hour all-hours-above-threshold continuation lower when the preceding row is calm (cbwd=cv), the index row has a named direction, and Iws rises, compared with eligible episodes without that transition?
candidates.new_claim: Adds an episode-level six-hour continuation estimand and a calm-to-named-direction plus rising-Iws contrast to the supplied regression framing. The current computation did not support the predicted reduction; the revised idea is to test whether this contrast is reproducible under better measurement of local wind and missingness.
candidates.input_delta: Thresholded episodes, one index per episode, the transition exposure, six-hour continuation, and prospective replication are additions; the input supplies hourly concentrations and airport meteorology but not this estimand.
candidates.domain_value: Could establish whether a simple wind-regime observation deserves evaluation as a cue for continued monitoring during high-pollution episodes.
assumptions: Consecutive No values denote consecutive hours.
Recorded cv and Iws changes are imperfect wind-regime proxies, not direct measures of local transport or dilution.
The 150 ug/m^3 threshold, six-hour horizon, and exposure definition are operational choices.
Missing PM2.5 can split observed episodes and complete-window selection can bias the contrast.

variables_and_units.exposure: previous cbwd=cv, index cbwd!=cv, and index Iws greater than previous Iws
variables_and_units.outcome: all six subsequent observed hourly PM2.5 values >=150 ug/m^3

candidates.testable_prediction: The preregistered directional prediction remains lower continuation after exposure, but C1 did not establish it; a prospective test should estimate the same risk difference with uncertainty and assess year/site transfer.
candidates.alternative: The contrast is near zero, reverses, or depends on missing-hour handling because the apparent relationship reflects episode selection, synoptic conditions, emissions, or imperfect wind measurement.
candidates.discriminating_test: At multiple sites, collect co-located hourly PM2.5, local wind speed/direction, boundary-layer height, monitor-status logs, and emissions/intervention timestamps. Freeze episode and exposure rules, include incomplete follow-up as censored rather than negative, and compare exposed versus matched unexposed episodes within site and season. Report support, overlap, risk difference and block uncertainty; test transfer in a held-out site or period.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: The descriptive contrast was computed; prospective measurement and causal/operational validation are not feasible from this single series.
candidates.required_new_data: Co-located monitor-level wind speed/direction and boundary-layer height, multiple PM2.5 sites, monitor status logs, emissions/intervention timestamps, and a prospective validation period.
candidates.failure_condition: Withdraw the directional persistence claim if adequately supported prospective comparisons show no meaningful negative risk difference, the result reverses across sites or periods, or reasonable missing-hour handling changes its sign.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search for Beijing or comparable urban PM2.5 episode duration/persistence conditioned on calm-to-directional wind transitions or rising wind speed, distinguishing this conditional estimand from concentration prediction and meteorological association.

candidates.title: Are missing PM2.5 hours concentrated around episode boundaries?
candidates.question: Do missing PM2.5 labels occur more often adjacent to observed transitions into or out of high-PM2.5 episodes than in seasonally and meteorologically comparable hours away from boundaries?
candidates.new_claim: Adds a boundary-relative sensor-coverage diagnostic: missingness could obscure episode onset or recovery and alter duration summaries.
candidates.input_delta: The input reports 2,067 missing labels among 43,824 rows; the boundary-relative contrast and its effect on episode summaries are proposed additions.
candidates.domain_value: Could identify whether monitoring gaps cluster near episode transitions and guide uptime audits.
assumptions: The regular row sequence identifies hourly missingness.
Observed episode boundaries are imperfect because status during missing hours is unknown.
Comparable calendar and meteorological strata have adequate support.

variables_and_units.boundary_window: within two hours of an observed crossing of 150 ug/m^3

candidates.testable_prediction: Missing-label frequency is higher within the prespecified two-hour boundary window than among matched non-boundary hours.
candidates.alternative: Missingness is unrelated to boundary proximity after adjustment, or apparent enrichment is induced by defining boundaries only where values are observed.
candidates.discriminating_test: Define crossings using adjacent observed values, compare missingness in the fixed window to matched hours, and report sensitivity to one declared alternative window plus the count of potentially split or uncertain episodes.
candidates.required_new_data: Monitor maintenance, calibration, and instrument-status logs.
candidates.failure_condition: The hypothesis fails if matched missingness is not elevated and plausible assignments to missing hours do not materially alter boundary counts.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search for missingness or downtime analyses in hourly air-quality episodes, especially tests near threshold crossings.

candidates.title: Does recorded wet-weather duration add episode-clearance information?
candidates.question: Among high-PM2.5 episode-hours, do positive recorded cumulative rain or snow hours (Ir or Is) predict lower PM2.5 at the next observed hour than dry hours matched on season, temperature, dew point, pressure, wind, and recent PM2.5?
candidates.new_claim: Adds an episode-conditioned wet-weather contrast testing incremental clearance information in supplied cumulative precipitation-duration fields, without claiming causal scavenging.
candidates.input_delta: Ir and Is are documented, but this episode-clearance estimand is not.
candidates.domain_value: Could show whether readily available weather fields help anticipate short-term episode changes and whether direct precipitation measurements are warranted.
assumptions: Ir and Is encode relevant recent wet-weather duration consistently enough for a predictive contrast.
The next observed hour is not an independent environmental replicate.
candidates.testable_prediction: Within supported matched episode-hours, Ir>0 or Is>0 is associated with a more negative next-observed-hour PM2.5 change than Ir=0 and Is=0.
candidates.alternative: No incremental difference remains after matching, or Ir/Is track seasonal or synoptic conditions rather than wet-weather clearance.
candidates.discriminating_test: Estimate separate rain and snow contrasts, freeze matching and gap rules, compare with a measured-weather baseline, and test temporal transfer by year; interpret as predictive association only.
candidates.required_new_data: Hourly precipitation amount/intensity, boundary-layer height, multiple PM2.5 sites, and emissions/intervention records for mechanistic attribution.
candidates.failure_condition: The contrast fails if overlap is sparse, association is absent or reverses under year holdout, or its sign depends on handling PM2.5 gaps.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Search prior analyses of rain/snow duration and short-horizon PM2.5 episode clearance, separating prediction from wet-scavenging claims.

task.deliverable: R1 refined I1 to one index per observed episode, returned one computation and one targeted Crossref search; L2 assessed the outputs and specified the next falsifiable test.
acceptance: Preserve the original directional prediction and distinguish it from the observed estimate.
Report support, matching and uncertainty without causal interpretation.
Use search titles only as leads and do not assert literature novelty without substantive comparison.
task.proposed_computation: Completed C1 on the supplied full DF: episode-level support and prespecified matched six-hour continuation contrast.
task.proposed_search: Completed S1 Crossref title search for Beijing/China PM2.5 episode persistence and wind transitions; coverage was limited and titles only.

critique: R1: repeated episode-hours can inflate support; use one index per episode.
R1: six-hour complete-label restriction can select episodes and missingness can split them; do not count missing follow-up as a negative outcome.
R1: measured weather and recent PM2.5 do not address emissions, boundary-layer height, spatial transport, or monitor mismatch; this single series cannot identify a causal effect.
R1: five calendar years make month-block uncertainty fragile; report year-specific support/sign only where adequate.

final.what_changed: R1 narrowed I1 from episode-hours to one index per observed episode after identifying pseudoreplication and selection risks. C1 returned a small matched difference with wide uncertainty, so the predicted directional pattern is not supported here. The idea is redirected to prospective, multi-site, missingness-aware validation rather than an operational wind rule.
final.what_is_known: C1 reports 576 eligible episodes (71 exposed, 505 controls), 71 matched pairs, unmatched continuation rates 0.2817 exposed and 0.3782 controls, matched exposed-minus-control difference -0.0141, and month-block percentile interval [-0.1408, 0.1250]. The estimate is compatible with no difference and does not establish a wind effect. S1 returned eight title/date/DOI-only records, including 'Episode-Based Evolution Pattern Analysis of Haze Pollution: Method Development and Results from Beijing, China'; no abstract or full text was supplied. Search coverage is limited, so world novelty remains unresolved.
final.what_is_new_hypothesis: A reproducible, locally measured calm-to-directional wind transition with increasing wind speed may identify a lower six-hour probability of remaining above 150 ug/m^3 during an already-high episode; this is a proposal only and the current estimate offers no clear support.
final.falsifier: An adequately supported prospective multi-site test yields no meaningful negative matched risk difference, reverses across sites/periods, or changes sign under plausible missing-hour handling.
final.minimum_next_test: Preregister threshold, horizon, exposure, censoring/missingness rules, matching and a meaningful-effect criterion; collect hourly co-located PM2.5, local wind and boundary-layer height plus monitor-status records at multiple sites; estimate site/season-matched episode-level risk differences with temporal block uncertainty and hold out a site or period. A confidence interval spanning zero is inconclusive unless it also rules out the prespecified meaningful decrease.
final.nearest_work_comparison: S1's title-only results include a Beijing haze episode evolution analysis, a potentially relevant prior-work lead. The titles do not establish whether the exact one-index-per-episode conditional transition contrast has been studied. No detailed findings or novelty conclusion can be inferred from these records.
final.novelty_status: Input-level increment: explicit one-index-per-episode six-hour continuation estimand and calm-to-directional-plus-rising-Iws exposure, beyond generic regression. World-literature novelty is unresolved; the related Beijing episode-analysis title is a lead and the search was not exhaustive.
limitations: Single monitoring series paired with airport meteorology; wind may not represent conditions at the PM monitor.
No emissions, intervention, boundary-layer-height, monitor-status, or multi-site measures; confounding and transport cannot be resolved.
Complete-follow-up restriction can select episodes, and missing PM2.5 can split observed episodes.
The month-block interval is fragile with five years; the code reports no covariate balance diagnostic or site/year holdout.
The computed descriptive association cannot establish causation or operational value.
